examples: chunk size larger than the list
deal these names into groups of two
break this list into batches of 3

skills.name: countItems
skills.card:
countItems — Count how many times each item appears in a list, ranked most common first.
  needs: items: array
  optional: ignoreCase: boolean
  e.g. "count how many of each are in this list" → {"items":["red","blue","red","green","red"]}
examples: count how many of each are in this list
tally a list where everything is different

skills.name: dedupeList
skills.card:
dedupeList — Remove repeated items from a list, keeping the first of each and the original order.
  needs: items: array
  optional: ignoreCase: boolean
  e.g. "remove the duplicates from this list" → {"items":["apple","banana","apple","cherry"]}
examples: remove the duplicates from this list
dedupe a list with nothing repeated
take the repeated entries out of this list
drop the repeats and keep each item once

skills.name: differenceLists
skills.card:
differenceLists — Find what is in one list but not the other, in both directions.
  needs: first: array, second: array
  optional: ignoreCase: boolean
  e.g. "what is in the first list but not the second" → {"first":["a","b","c"],"second":["b"]}
examples: what is in the first list but not the second
compare these two lists of numbers
are these two lists the same
which entries are only in one of these
difference between two name lists ignoring case

skills.name: flattenList
skills.card:
flattenList — Flatten a list of nested lists into a single flat list.
  needs: items: array
  optional: depth: integer
  e.g. "flatten this nested list" → {"items":[1,[2,3],[4,[5]]]}

items.label: list
items.prompt: Which nested list should I flatten?

depth.label: levels to flatten
depth.description: how many levels to flatten — all of them by default

skills.name: intersectLists
skills.card:
intersectLists — Keep only the items appearing on both lists.
  needs: first: array, second: array
  optional: ignoreCase: boolean
  e.g. "what is in both of these lists" → {"first":["apple","banana","cherry"],"second":["banana","cherry","date"]}
examples: what is in both of these lists
do these two lists overlap at all
names in both lists ignoring case
common items where the first list repeats one
which items show up in both list a and list b
what do these two lists have in common

skills.name: pairUp
skills.card:
pairUp — Draw people into random pairs or teams from a seed.
  needs: items: array, seed: integer
  optional: groupSize: integer
  e.g. "pair these four people up, seed 7" → {"items":["Ana","Bo","Cy","Di"],"seed":7}

items.label: list
items.prompt: Who or what should I pair up?

seed.label: repeatable seed
seed.prompt: Which seed? Any whole number — the same seed always draws the same pairs.

examples: pair these four people up, seed 7
draw pairs from five names, seed 1
split six into teams of three, seed 42
secret santa draw for three, seed 9

skills.name: pickRandom
skills.card:
pickRandom — Pick one or more items at random from a list, from a seed so the pick can be repeated.
  needs: items: array, seed: integer
  optional: count: integer, allowRepeats: boolean
  e.g. "pick one of these at random with seed 7" → {"items":["tea","coffee","water"],"seed":7}

items.label: list
items.prompt: Which list should I pick from?

seed.label: repeatable seed
seed.prompt: Which seed? Any whole number — the same seed always picks the same thing.

examples: pick one of these at random with seed 7
choose a name from the list, seed 1
pick from a one item list

skills.name: rangeList
skills.card:
rangeList — Count from one number to another in steps, listing every number on the way.
  needs: from: number, to: number
  optional: step: number
  e.g. "list the numbers 1 to 5" → {"from":1,"to":5}
examples: a range where start and end are the same
list the multiples of five between 5 and 40
count from 10 down to 0 in twos

skills.name: shuffleList

seed.label: repeatable seed
seed.prompt: Which seed? Any whole number — the same seed always gives the same order.

examples: shuffle the running order with seed 42
mix these into a random order with seed 2

skills.name: sortList
skills.card:
sortList — Put a list of items in order — alphabetically, numerically, or in natural order where numbers inside names count.
  needs: items: array
  optional: by: string, direction: string
  e.g. "sort this list alphabetically" → {"items":["cherry","apple","banana"]}
examples: sort file names in natural order
order these names z to a

skills.name: unionLists
skills.card:
unionLists — Merge two lists into one, dropping repeats.
  needs: first: array, second: array
  optional: ignoreCase: boolean
  e.g. "combine these two lists" → {"first":["a","b"],"second":["b","c"]}
examples: combine two name lists ignoring case

skills.name: zipLists
skills.card:
zipLists — Combine two or more lists position by position — pair each name with its score.
  needs: lists: array
  optional: names: array, strict: boolean
  e.g. "zip these two lists together" → {"lists":[[1,2,3],["a","b","c"]]}

names.label: field names
names.description: a name for each list, to build objects instead of rows

strict.label: equal lengths only
strict.description: refuse when the lists are different lengths

examples: combine names and ages into records
match each name up with the corresponding score
line these two lists up side by side

skills.name: breakEvenComparison
skills.card:
breakEvenComparison — Find the point at which one option starts to pay off against another.
  needs: fixedA: number, perUnitA: number, fixedB: number, perUnitB: number
  optional: nameA: string, nameB: string
  e.g. "when does the subscription beat paying per use" → {"fixedA":100,"perUnitA":5,"fixedB":0,"perUnitB":10}

fixedA.label: first option up front
fixedA.prompt: What does the first option cost up front?

fixedB.label: second option up front
fixedB.prompt: What does the second option cost up front?

examples: when does the subscription beat paying per use
break even between buying and renting
is there a break even point here
break even on a cheaper machine with pricier supplies
